page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 32 vCPUs and 32 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via three NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 144 GB of VRAM.

In benchmark testing, this configuration demonstrates top-tier performance across multiple dimensions. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top 10% placement in both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as Geekbench and Passmark CPU evaluations. Memory performance is strong, with uncached read bandwidth reaching 331.99 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 123.17 GB/sec. The system also excels in data processing, recording top-tier results in Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput.

The triple NVIDIA L40S GPU setup delivers high-throughput capabilities for artificial intelligence workloads. LLM inference benchmarks show top-tier execution, processing 13662.51 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model and 6061.83 tokens per second on a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds reach 495.42 tokens per second and 129.38 tokens per second for the 135M and 7B models, respectively.

Notable architectural tradeoffs include a shared CPU allocation model and the complete absence of local storage, meaning external storage solutions must be utilized. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU resources and system memory relative to the virtual core count offers a consolidated platform for resource-intensive deployments. This server is suited for large-scale LLM inference, machine learning model training, high-performance computing, data science pipelines, and complex database operations.
